text:
olivia_support: FYI customer 'AcmeMaps' (org: acme-01) opened an escalation — they see repeated 429s yesterday evening even though the project quota tile shows ~40% available. invoice for March also shows ~2.3M tokens used whereas the dashboard shows ~1.9M. can we triage?

ben_oncall: ack. do we have the org vs project ids and a sample request id that hit 429?

olivia_support: org=acme-01, project=acme-01-prod, customer supplied one request id: req_2026-03-15_84321. They said it happened between 18:10-18:45 UTC. Logs attached by customer: "HTTP 429 Rate limit exceeded" + header dump.

matt_prod: thanks. first thought: rolling-window enforcement might've counted some shared-pool traffic at org level, but project tile shows project-local quota — could be mismatch in aggregation path. i'll pull the enforcement logs for that window.

kevin_data: tagging metering-bot to surface ledger vs realtime gaps @metering-bot 

metering-bot: queued job metering.diff_check for acme-01 (window 2026-03-15T18:00:00Z -> 2026-03-15T19:00:00Z). ETA ~90s.

ben_oncall: while we wait, any quick repro to reproduce counting? is the customer using embeddings + text gen in same project? sometimes cross-tenant calls route differently.

olivia_support: yes they said embeddings burst from background job + foreground chat requests. background jobs run under the same project key though.

matt_prod: found enforcement logs. At 18:12:03 we enforced a org-level shared-pool throttle because org rolling-window count breached org burst threshold. project tile still showed available because project-level rolling window didn't cross its own limit. so request got 429 due to org-level policy.

kevin_data: metering-bot results:
```
metering-bot: ledger_tokens=1,920,412
metering-bot: realtime_tokens=2,143,987
metering-bot: delta=223,575 (11.6% higher realtime)
```
The realtime stream includes some short-lived retry duplicates and background-worker batching expansion which the ledger pipeline de-dupes later.

sophie_billing: invoice pipeline uses ledger aggregates (post-de-dupe). invoice shows 2.3M — that's larger than both? can you paste the invoice line item id?

olivia_support: invoice line item id: inv_ln_2026_03_acme_01_43. they pasted a screenshot: invoice summary line = 2,301,220 tokens.

kevin_data: OK that suggests there was a late reprocessing batch that increased ledger count after the initial ledger snapshot we queried. our ledger snapshot timestamp for the dashboard tile is the microbatch commit_ts; dashboards query a cached snapshot that may be up to ~10 minutes stale depending on cache TTL.

matt_prod: tl;dr: timeline we believe: realtime pipeline inflated (retries) -> enforcement triggered at org-level (counting events in enforcement stream) -> later ledger reprocessing added additional tokens (billing) -> dashboard cached tile used earlier microbatch snapshot -> invoice used latest ledger resulting in higher number. that explains both the 429s and invoice vs dashboard delta.

ben_oncall: can we reproduce exact spike? what's the query to look at the enforcement stream and last-mile ledger entries for that org?

kevin_data: here's a query we ran (pseudo SQL):
```
SELECT ts, event_type, project, org, tokens
FROM enforcement_stream
WHERE org = 'acme-01' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-15T18:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-15T19:00:00Z'
ORDER BY ts;
```
and ledger diff: 
```
SELECT commit_ts, sum(tokens) FROM ledger_events
WHERE org='acme-01' AND commit_ts BETWEEN '2026-03-15' AND '2026-03-16'
GROUP BY commit_ts ORDER BY commit_ts;
```

kevin_data: enforcement stream shows a burst of ~250k tokens at 18:12-18:14 from project acme-01-batch (they thought it was acme-01-prod but we see batch job key). that pushed org window over threshold and enforcement acted on other projects under the same org.

olivia_support: customer insists batch job is in a separate project but they used the same org-level key for cross-project calls. they said "we thought project isolation would prevent this".

matt_prod: note: org-level shared pool is intended to protect orgs from runaway projects; if multiple projects share org pool, burst from one project can cause 429s in another. might be a docs gap.

sophie_billing: on the invoice discrepancy — i'll open a billing probe to validate invoice line reconciles to ledger increments and timestamp of last reprocess. if ledger reprocessed after dashboard snapshot, that matches. i'll report back with invoice-run-id.

ben_oncall: immediate mitigation for customer: we can lift org-level throttle for 1 hour or grant the project a dedicated quota while they fix their batch job keys. but both options need approvals.

olivia_support: customer asked for temporary bypass. they granted support access. can we do a 1-hour org bypass?

matt_prod: we have a playbook. planned steps: 1) set org-level override to allow acc=acme-01 for 1h, 2) monitor enforcement metrics for 10m, 3) confirm 429s stop, 4) revert. I'll schedule at 20:30 UTC if support OK.

sophie_billing: billing probe created: bill-probe-1975314820-acme-01. expected final in 2-4h.

kevin_data: followup action for infra: add event-tagging mapping check to prevent background batch jobs from using project keys that are meant to be separate. also consider smaller cache TTL for project-level tiles when ledger reprocesses are frequent.

olivia_support: thanks all. customer notified about cause (org shared-pool burst) and offered temporary bypass + guidance to separate keys. i'll update ticket with timeline and the enforcement log snippet we captured. :thumbsup:

matt_prod: i'll run the bypass at planned time and ping here once done.

ben_oncall: nice triage. marking this thread for postmortem if billing probe shows unexpected ledger reprocessing pattern.

olivia_support: closing loop for now — will reopen if customer still sees 429s after bypass.
